Rashi on Pesachim 63a:1:1.english: And in accordance with Rava - In the second chapter of Zevachim.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:1:2.hebrew: עדיין היא מחלוקת - גבי "תפוס לשון ראשון", דאיפלגי בה ר' מאיר ור' יוסי באומר "הרי זו תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים" — הרי זו תמורת עולה, דברי רבי מאיר, דתפוס לשון ראשון; רבי יוסי אומר: דבריו קיימים, דאף בגמר דבריו אדם נתפס. ואיבעיא להו: אמר "חציה עולה וחציה שלמים", מי מודה בה ר' מאיר או לא? מי אמרינן טעמא דרבי מאיר משום דנמלך הוא, וכיון דחל שם עולה תו לא פקע, אבל כי אמר לחצאין ליכא למימר הכי; או דילמא כיון דפשטא ביה קדושת עולה ברישא תו לא חיילא קדושת שלמים? ואמר אביי: בהא ודאי מודי ר"מ. רבא אמר: עדיין היא מחלוקת. ואותביה רבא לאביי מ"השוחט את הזבח לאכול כזית בחוץ כזית למחר", דקא פליג ר' יהודה אדרבנן ואמר כר' מאיר "תפוס לשון ראשון", דקאמר: זה הכלל, כל שמחשבת זמן קדמה למחשבת מקום — פיגול וחייבין עליו כרת, לא שנא בעבודה אחת ולא שנא בשתי עבודות; שחישב בעבודה שניה מחשבת פסול בתר מחשבת פיגול, לא מפקע ליה מיד פיגול, דתפוס לשון ראשון. ורבנן סברי אף בגמר דבריו הוא נתפס, והויא לה בחדא עבודה עירוב מחשבות, ולא קרב המתיר כמצוותו, ואנן בעינן דלא ליהוי ביה פסול אחרינא, דהרצאה כתיב ביה. אלמא מאן דאית ליה תפוס לשון ראשון אפילו לחצאין אית ליה, דהא זיתי טובא יש בזבח, ופליג ר' יהודה. ואמר ליה אביי: מי סברת אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף וחדא מחשבה היא? ישנה לשחיטה מתחלה ועד סוף כו', וכגון דאמר סימן ראשון חוץ לזמנו ושני חוץ למקומו, ור"מ סבר מפגלין בסימן אחד. מכלל דרבא דאותביה מהא ס"ל אליבא דר' מאיר ור' יהודה דאינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף, וכולה מחשבה בסוף שחיטה הוא והוה ליה חדא מחשבה, ונמלך ליכא למימר דהא בשני זיתים חישב, ואפילו הכי פליג. והיינו דאמרינן הכא: לימא קסברי אחרים אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף, וכל מחשבת שחיטה לא מהניא אלא אם כן חישב בגמרה, וכדרבא דאמר התם "עדיין היא מחלוקת" באומר לחצאין, וע"כ אית ליה לרבי מאיר אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף, ואחרים היינו ר"מ. הילכך, בגמר שחיטה אין שהות לומר שני דברים, והיכא דהקדים מולין לערלים בסוף שחיטה, מולין חיילי כולה; הקדים ערלים למולין, ערלים חיילי כולה, והוה ליה כולה ערלה ופסלה:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:1:2.english: It is still a dispute - Regarding [the principle of] "grasp the first expression," about which Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei disagreed concerning one who says, "Behold, this is a substitute for a burnt-offering, a substitute for a peace-offering": [It is] a substitute for a burnt-offering, [these are] the words of Rabbi Meir, for we grasp the first expression; Rabbi Yosei says: His words stand, for a person is held [accountable] even for the conclusion of his words. And it was asked of them: If he said, "Half of it is a burnt-offering and half of it is a peace-offering," does Rabbi Meir concede in this [case] or not? Do we say [that] Rabbi Meir's reason [in the first case] is because he changed his mind, and once the status of a burnt-offering took effect [on the animal], it does not subsequently leave [it], whereas when he spoke in halves one cannot say this; or perhaps, since the sanctity of a burnt-offering spread through it first, the sanctity of a peace-offering cannot subsequently take effect? And Abaye said: In this [case], Rabbi Meir certainly concedes. Rava said: It is still a dispute. And Rava raised an objection against Abaye from [the Mishnah]: "One who slaughters the sacrifice to eat an olive's bulk outside [its proper place, and] an olive's bulk the next day," where Rabbi Yehudah disagrees with the Rabbis and rules in accordance with Rabbi Meir [who holds] "grasp the first expression." For [the Mishnah] states: This is the general rule: Whenever an intent of time precedes an intent of place, it is piggul, and one is liable to karet for it — whether in one service or in two services; [that is, if] he had an invalidating intent during the second service after a piggul intent [during the first], it does not remove it from the category of piggul, because we grasp the first expression. Whereas the Rabbis hold [that] a person is held [accountable] even for the conclusion of his words, so there is in one service a mixture of intents, and the permitting [rite] was not offered according to its commandment — and we require that there be no other disqualification in it, for "acceptance" (hartza'ah) is written regarding it. Thus, [we see that] the one who holds "grasp the first expression" holds [it] even [when spoken] in halves, for there are many olive's bulks in a sacrifice, and yet Rabbi Yehudah disagrees [with the Rabbis]! And Abaye said to him: Do you think slaughter is only at the end and it is one [single] intent? Slaughter is [considered to take place] from the beginning to the end, etc., and [the Mishnah is] a case where he expressed [an intent of] outside its time [during the cutting of] the first siman [organ], and outside its place [during] the second, and Rabbi Meir holds that one renders [a sacrifice] piggul [even] in one siman. It follows that Rava, who raised an objection against him from this [Mishnah], holds according to Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehudah that slaughter is only at the end, and the entire intent is at the end of the slaughter, so it is one intent — and one cannot say [he] "changed his mind," since he intended regarding two [separate] olive's bulks — and even so, [Rabbi Yehudah] disagrees! And this is what [the Gemara] says here: "Let us say that Aḥerim hold that slaughter is only at the end," and any intent during slaughter is effective only if one had the intent at its completion, in accordance with Rava who said there, "It is still a dispute," regarding one who speaks in halves — and perforce Rabbi Meir holds that slaughter is only at the end, and Aḥerim is Rabbi Meir. Therefore, at the completion of the slaughter there is no time to say two things; and where he placed circumcised [owners] before uncircumcised [owners] at the end of the slaughter, "circumcised" takes effect for all of it; [if] he placed uncircumcised before circumcised, "uncircumcised" takes effect for all of it, so all of it is [for] uncircumcised [owners] and it is disqualified:

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:3:1.hebrew: והכא במאי עסקינן - דקתני הקדים ערלים למולין פסול, כגון שגמר בלבו להוציא מולין אחר ערלים ולומר "לערלים ולמולין". כל מחשבה דקדשים מוציא בפיו הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:3:1.english: And with what are we dealing here - where it teaches [that if] he put uncircumcised before circumcised, it is invalid? [With a case] where he resolved in his mind to express "circumcised" after "uncircumcised" and to say, "For uncircumcised and for circumcised." [For] any intention regarding consecrated [offerings] is [one that] he expresses with his mouth.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:4:1.hebrew: לא בעינן פיו ולבו שוין - והלך אחר פיו, ואיכא כולה ערלה, ואע"פ שלא היה בלבו אלא למקצתה:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:4:1.english: We do not require his mouth and heart [to be] the same - And follow his mouth, so that all of it [the slaughter] is [for] the uncircumcised, even though in his heart [his intent was] only for part of it.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:4:2.english: That I will not derive benefit from this [one] - From this man.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:4:3.hebrew: לא אמר כלום - וסתם משנה היא, ור"מ היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:4:3.english: He has not said anything - And it is an unattributed Mishnah, and it is [the view of] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:5:1.hebrew: סימן שני אף לערלים - גרסינן. בסימן ראשון לא היה דעתו אלא למה שהוציא בפיו, ובסימן שני היה מוסיף על מחשבתו. הילכך, כי הקדים ערלים למולין, נגמר סימן ראשון בערלים:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:5:1.english: The second organ even for uncircumcised people - This is our textual reading. During [the cutting of] the first organ, his intention was only for what he expressed with his mouth, and during [the cutting of] the second organ, he was adding to his thought. Therefore, when he placed uncircumcised people before circumcised people, the first organ was completed [solely] for uncircumcised people.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:6:1.hebrew: ור' מאיר לטעמיה דאמר - במנחות, מפגלין בחצי מתיר; דתנן: פיגל בקומץ ולא בלבונה, בלבונה ולא בקומץ — כלומר, חישב בהקטרת האחד על מנת לאכול מן השיריים למחר — ר"מ אומר: פיגול, וחכ"א: אין בו כרת עד שיפגל בכל המתיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:6:1.english: And Rabbi Meir [follows] his [own] reasoning, as he says - In [tractate] Menachot, [that] piggul status can be conferred at half of what renders [the offering] permitted, as we learned [in a Mishnah]: If one intended piggul regarding the handful [of meal-offering] but not regarding the frankincense, [or] regarding the frankincense but not regarding the handful — that is to say, he had an improper intent during the burning of one [of them] in order to eat from the remainder the next day — Rabbi Meir says: It is piggul; and the Sages say: There is no karet for it unless he intends piggul during the entire [act] that renders [it] permitted.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:6:2.hebrew: יש פיגול - במחשבת חצי מתיר. והאי חצי מתיר הוא, דשחיטה בשני הסימנין היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:6:2.english: There is piggul - through an intention [during] half of what renders [the offering] permitted. And this [case] is [also] half of what renders [it] permitted, for slaughter is [performed] on the two simanim [the windpipe and esophagus].

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:1.english: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread violates a negative commandment - For [it is written], "You shall not slaughter with leavened bread," etc.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:2.hebrew: אף התמיד - של בין הערבים דערב הפסח ששחטו על החמץ, וטעמא יליף בגמ':
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:2.english: Even the daily offering - [That] of the afternoon of Passover eve, which one slaughtered with leaven [in his possession]; and [the Gemara] derives the reason in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:3.hebrew: ר"ש אומר הפסח בי"ד - ששחטו על החמץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:3.english: Rabbi Shimon says: The Paschal lamb on the fourteenth - That he slaughtered it with leavened bread [in his possession].

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:4.hebrew: לשמו חייב - משום לא תשחט על חמץ, דפסח כשר הוא ושחיטה ראויה היא (ושמה שחיטה):
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:4.english: For its [own] purpose, [he is] liable - On account of "You shall not slaughter with leaven," for it is a valid Paschal offering and it is a proper slaughter (and it is called slaughter).

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:5.hebrew: ושלא לשמו פטור - דפסול הוא, ושחיטה שאינה ראויה לאו שמה שחיטה. והכי אית ליה לר"ש בכל דוכתי — בכיסוי הדם (חולין דף פה.), ובאותו ואת בנו (דף פא:), ובתשלומי ארבעה וחמשה (ב"ק ע.):
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:5.english: And [if slaughtered] not for its own purpose, he is exempt - For it is disqualified, and a slaughter that is not fit [to permit the animal] is not deemed a slaughter. And so does Rabbi Shimon hold everywhere: regarding covering the blood (Chullin 85a), and regarding "it and its young" (81b), and regarding the fourfold and fivefold payment (Bava Kamma 70a).

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:6.hebrew: ושאר כל הזבחים - ששחטן בי"ד לאחר חצות על החמץ, בין לשמן ושלא לשמן, ואע"ג שכשירין הן, כדתנן (זבחים דף ב.): כל הזבחים שנזבחו שלא לשמן כשירין:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:6.english: And all other offerings - That one slaughtered on the fourteenth [of Nisan] after midday with leavened bread [in his possession], whether for their own purpose or not for their own purpose — even though they are valid, as we learned in the Mishnah (Zevachim 2a): "All offerings that were slaughtered not for their own purpose are valid."

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:7.hebrew: פטור - כדמפרש בגמ', בעידנא דמחייב אפסח, לא מיחייב אשאר זבחים:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:7:7.english: He is exempt - As [it] explains in the Gemara: at the time when one is liable for the Paschal lamb, he is not liable for other offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:1.hebrew: ובמועד - בתוך הפסח, אם לשמו שחטו לפסח על החמץ, פטור מ"לא תשחט", דפסח שלא בזמנו לשמו פסול, והויא לה שחיטה שאינה ראויה:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:1.english: And during the festival - Within Passover, if one slaughtered it for its [own] purpose, as a Paschal offering, with leaven [in his possession], he is exempt from [the prohibition of] "You shall not slaughter," because a Paschal offering [slaughtered] not in its [proper] time for its [own] purpose is disqualified, and it is [considered] an unfit slaughter.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:2.english: Not for its own sake - Rather, for the sake of a peace-offering.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:3.english: And all other offerings - That he slaughtered during the festival with leaven [in his possession].

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:4.hebrew: בין לשמן בין כו' חייב - דהא כשירין הן, ובגמ' מפרש דקרא אשאר זבחים נמי אזהר:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:4.english: Whether for their [own] purpose, whether etc., he is liable - For behold, they are valid, and in the Gemara [it] explains that the verse also warned regarding other offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:5.hebrew: חוץ מן החטאת ששחטה שלא לשמה - דפסולה היא, כדתנן בזבחים (שם): "חוץ מן הפסח והחטאת". וטעמא, משום דכתיב בשחיטה "חטאת היא" — מעוטא: היא, ולא הנשחטת שלא לשמה:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:8:5.english: Except for a sin-offering that he slaughtered for a different purpose - For it is disqualified, as we learned in a Mishnah in Zevachim (ibid.): "Except for the Paschal lamb and the sin-offering." And the reason is because it is written regarding [its] slaughtering, "It is a sin-offering" — [which is] an exclusion: "it" [when slaughtered for its own purpose], and not one that is slaughtered for a different purpose.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:9:1.hebrew: עד שיהא החמץ לשוחט כו' - ואע"ג דכתיב על חמץ סתמא, אם היה חמץ לאחד שאינו מבני החבורה — ואפילו ישנו עמו בעזרה, ואלו השוחטין פסחיהן רואין אותו והתרו בהן — אין עוברין, כדמפרש לקמיה, מדכתיב לא תשחט ולא ילין: כל שישנו בהלנה ישנו בשחיטה. ואם יש לא' מהן, כולן עוברין:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:9:1.english: Unless the leavened bread belongs to the one who slaughters, etc. - Even though [Scripture] writes "with leavened bread" unconditionally, if leavened bread belonged to someone who is not among the members of the company — even if he is with him in the Temple courtyard, and those slaughtering their Paschal lambs see him and were forewarned — they do not transgress, as [the Gemara] explains further on, since it is written: "You shall not slaughter ... and it shall not remain overnight" — anyone who is [subject to the prohibition] of leaving [the offering] overnight is [subject to the prohibition] of slaughtering [with leavened bread]. And if one of them has [leavened bread], all of them transgress.

Rashi on Pesachim 63a:9:2.hebrew: לזורק - הדם, דזריקה נמי איתרביא במכילתא מדם זבחיך:
Rashi on Pesachim 63a:9:2.english: To the one who sprinkles - the blood, for sprinkling is also included in the Mekhilta from "the blood of Your sacrifice."

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:1:1.hebrew: לימא קסברי אחרים אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף וכדרבא וכו' - בפ' שני דזבחים (ד' ל.) פליגי אביי ורבא אליבא דר"מ, דאביי אמר בלחצו' מודה ר' מאיר, ורבא אמר עדיין היא מחלוקת, והתם נמי סבר ר' מאיר "תפוס לשון ראשון". ולחצות מפרש בקונטרס: חציה תמורת עולה וחציה תמורת שלמים. ונראה כפירוש ר"ח, דמפרש לחצות — לחצי היום יחולו שניהם; וקאמר אביי דהתם מודה ר"מ, כיון דבשעת אמירה אינם חלים, ולחצי היום יחולו שניהם. ורבא סבר דאפילו התם פליג רבי מאיר, כמו בשחיטה דאינה אלא לבסוף, דאין כאן אלא משהו אחד לחול לשניהם, ולר' מאיר חייל קמא. ולהכי לערלים ולמולים — ערלים חיילי, דאמרינן תפוס לשון ראשון. אבל אי ישנה לשחיטה מתחלה ועד סוף, כיון שיש שהות לשניהם לחול — חיילי תרווייהו, ולא אמרינן תפוס לשון ראשון; אלא דוקא אי אמרינן אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף, דאין להם שהות לחול לשניהם כדפרי'. ולא דמי לתמורת עולה ותמורת שלמים, דיותר אמרינן תפוס לשון ראשון כי לא אמר לחצות — שיש לשניהם שהות לחול — מכי אמר לחצות; דהתם, כיון דאמר תמורת עולה ואפילו חציה, פשטה בכולה, ותו לא מצי חייל תמורת שלמים. אבל מולים וערלים, כי אמרי ישנה לשחיטה כו', הואיל ויכולים לחול זה אחר זה, חיילי תרוייהו, אף על גב דסבירא ליה בעלמא תפוס לשון ראשון:
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:1:1.english: "Let us say that Aḥerim hold that slaughter is not [legally significant] until the end, in accordance with Rava, etc." - In the second chapter of Zevachim (30a), Abaye and Rava disagree according to Rabbi Meir: for Abaye says that in the case of "at midday" [lachatzot], Rabbi Meir concedes, whereas Rava says it is still a dispute; and there too Rabbi Meir holds "follow the first expression" [tafos lashon rishon]. Now, lachatzot [lit. to divide] is explained in the Kuntres [Rashi] as: half of it is a substitute for a burnt-offering and half of it is a substitute for a peace-offering. However, it appears [more accurate] like the explanation of Rabbeinu Chananel, who explains lachatzot [to mean]: at midday [lachatzi hayom] both shall take effect; and Abaye says that there Rabbi Meir concedes, since at the time of the utterance they do not take effect, and at midday both will take effect [simultaneously]. But Rava holds that even there Rabbi Meir disagrees, just as with slaughter, which is only [effective] at the very end, where there is only one tiny moment for both to take effect, and according to Rabbi Meir the first one takes effect. Therefore, [when one slaughters] for uncircumcised and for circumcised people, [the intent for] uncircumcised takes effect, because we say "follow the first expression." However, if slaughter is [an ongoing process] from beginning to end, since there is time for both of them to take effect, both take effect, and we do not say "follow the first expression"; [rather, we say it] only specifically if we say that slaughter is not [effective] until the end, when they do not have time for both to take effect, as I have explained. And this is not comparable to [the case of] a substitute for a burnt-offering and a substitute for a peace-offering, where we say "follow the first expression" even more when he did not say lachatzot—where both have time to take effect—than when he did say lachatzot; for there, once he said "a substitute for a burnt-offering," even [for] half of it, [the sanctity] spreads throughout the entire [animal], and the substitute for a peace-offering can no longer take effect. Whereas [with] circumcised and uncircumcised people, when we say "slaughter is [from beginning to end], etc.," since they can take effect one after the other, both take effect, even though he generally holds "follow the first expression."

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:3:1.hebrew: ולא הספיק לומר למולים כו' - תימה לרשב"א: א"כ, מאי איריא דקתני "הקדים מולים לערלים"? אפילו הקדים ערלים, כשר אם הספיק לומר "למולים" קודם גמר שחיטה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:3:1.english: And [he] did not have a chance to say "for circumcised people," etc. - [This] is astonishing to Rashba: if so, why did [the Tanna] specifically teach, "If he preceded circumcised [people] to uncircumcised [people]"? Even if he preceded uncircumcised [people], it is valid if he had a chance to say "for circumcised people" before the completion of the slaughter.

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:3:2.hebrew: רבי מאיר סבר לא בעינן פיו ולבו שוין - מכאן מדקדק ר"י, דהא דקרי בכל דוכתי "פיגול" פסול מחשבה — לאו דוקא, דאינו פיגול עד שיוציא בשפתיו; דאי במחשבה תליא מילתא, בשלא הספיק לומר "למולים", אמאי פסול לר' מאיר? הלא גמר בלבו נמי לומר "למולים":
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:3:2.english: Rabbi Meir holds we do not require that one's mouth and heart be the same - From here Ri infers that [the fact] that everywhere [the Talmud] calls piggul a "disqualification of thought" is not exact, for it is not piggul until one expresses [it] with his lips; for if the matter depended on thought, [then] when he did not have a chance to say "for circumcised people," why is it disqualified according to Rabbi Meir? Did he not also decide in his heart to say "for circumcised people"?

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:4:1.hebrew: המתכוין לומר תרומה כו' - אפילו אי דברים שבלב לא הוו דברים, גבי ההוא דזבין לניכסי' אדעתא למיסק לארץ ישראל ובעידנא דזבין לא אמר (קדושין דף מט:) — התם אינו טועה בדיבורו; אבל הכא דברים שבלב הם, ומה שהוציא בשפתיו אינו כלום, לפי שטעה בדיבורו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:4:1.english: "One who intended to say teruma," etc. - Even if matters in the heart [i.e., unspoken intentions] are not [considered] words — as in [the case of] that [man] who sold his property with the intention of ascending to the Land of Israel, and at the time he sold [it] he did not state [it] (Kiddushin 49b) — there, he is not erring in his speech; whereas here, [his intentions] are matters in the heart, and what he uttered with his lips is nothing, because he erred in his speech.

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:5:1.hebrew: וסימן שני אף לערלים דפתיכי מולין וכו' - וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי קאמר "הקדים מולין"? אפילו לא הקדים נמי, אלא ששחט סימן ראשון למולים ולערלים וכן שני! ואומר ר"י דקמ"ל, דאפילו לא פירש "אף לערלים", אלא ששחט שני לערלים סתמא — כיון ששחט סימן ראשון למולים, מסתמא "אף לערלים" קאמר. וכן בסיפא דקתני "ערלים למולים פסול" — אפילו הקדים מולין פסול, אם פירש שני לערלים דוקא; אלא הא קמ"ל, דאע"פ ששחט סימן ראשון לערלים סתם, לא אמרינן כיון ששחט סימן שני למולים גלי אדעתיה דבסימן ראשון "אף לערלים" קאמר וכשר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:5:1.english: And the second organ even for uncircumcised [people], so that circumcised [people] are included, etc. - And if you say: if so, why does it state '[if] he preceded with circumcised [people]'? Even if he did not precede [with them] as well, [it should be valid,] provided that he slaughtered the first organ for circumcised and for uncircumcised [people], and similarly the second! And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that it teaches us that even if he did not specify 'even for uncircumcised [people],' but rather slaughtered the second [organ] for uncircumcised [people] without specification — since he slaughtered the first organ for circumcised [people], presumably he meant 'even for uncircumcised [people].' And similarly in the latter clause, where it teaches 'uncircumcised [first, then] circumcised — invalid': even if he preceded with circumcised [people] it is invalid if he specified the second [organ] for uncircumcised [people] exclusively; rather, this is what it teaches us: that even though he slaughtered the first organ for uncircumcised [people] without specification, we do not say [that] since he slaughtered the second organ for circumcised [people], he revealed his intention that in the first organ he meant 'even for uncircumcised [people]' and it is valid.

Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:7:1.hebrew: השוחט פסח על החמץ עובר בלא תעשה - אומר ריב"א דהפסח כשר, דהא לא שנה עליו הכתוב לעכב. ובתוספתא דמכילתין (פ"ד) תניא בהדיא: "השוחט את הפסח על החמץ בי"ד — עובר בלא תעשה, והפסח עצמו כשר, ויוצא בו ידי חובתו בפסח":
Tosafot on Pesachim 63a:7:1.english: One who slaughters a Paschal lamb with leavened bread violates a negative commandment - Riva says that the Paschal lamb is valid, since Scripture did not repeat [the prohibition] concerning it to make it indispensable. And in the Tosefta of our tractate (Chapter 4), it is taught explicitly: "One who slaughters the Paschal lamb with leavened bread on the fourteenth [of Nisan] violates a negative commandment, yet the Paschal lamb itself is valid, and one fulfills his obligation with it on Passover."
